data.exact_reserve_text: There were no issues arising from our closed years being 2007 to 2012 and all of these years combined produced a surplus which contributed both to the calendar year result and the closing 2013 account result. At thirty-six months the account has produced a pure loss and prior year underwriting profit together with a small amount of investment income. Overall the result is a profit of $0.05 million (which equates to GBP 0.03 million) which is 0.1% of a stamp capacity of GBP 30 million.

prior_year_events.impact_description: one offshore energy loss of note, which attaches to our reinsurance programme. Although the new accounts produced less income than was originally planned, they have both been profitable and are now running off smoothly.

named_events.loss_description: one offshore energy loss of note, which attaches to our reinsurance programme.

named_events.event_name: collapse of the global oil price
named_events.loss_description: The dominant issue during the year, which has affected both our cargo and offshore energy lines, has been the collapse of the global oil price during 2015.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a significant release of prior year reserves, totaling $10.438 million. This favorable development stemmed from surpluses generated on closed years of account from 2007 to 2012, which contributed to the 2013 account result, and a profit on the 2014 account. The 2013 account, including movements from 2007-2012, produced a profit of $2.984 million, and the 2014 account generated a profit of $7.454 million. No specific events were detailed as driving these releases, but the 2014 account was noted as profitable despite an offshore energy loss, which was contained by reinsurance.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development is derived from the 'Profit for the financial year' breakdown by account year on page 3, which represents the gross profit for those prior years. LOB-specific movements for prior year development are not provided. The claims development triangle is presented in loss ratios, not absolute amounts, and therefore cannot be used to calculate absolute prior year development without underwriting year premiums.
